property_summary: For any caller who is not the current owner, a call to transferOwnership must revert and leave the owner unchanged; the mutant lets any caller set the owner, so for a non-owner actor and new owner the mutant's owner differs while the reference's stays the same.

After a successful transferOwnership call by the current owner, the owner must become the _newOwner argument for every fuzzed (actor, newOwner) pair; the mutant instead sets owner = msg.sender, which breaks this for any input where newOwner != actor.

For any caller who is the current owner and any nonzero new owner address, a completed transferOwnership call must leave owner equal to exactly the supplied argument; the mutant instead stores the zero address, violating owner == _newOwner for every nonzero argument.

Only the current owner may transfer ownership: a call to transferOwnership from any non-owner must revert and leave owner unchanged; the inverted modifier lets non-owners pass, so owner changes for some fuzzed caller.
For any caller that is not the current owner, calling transferOwnership must never change owner; the buggy version removes the onlyOwner check, so any caller can set owner to a new value.

Once ownership is transferred to A (the only party able to do so being the current owner), any subsequent transferOwnership call from a caller other than A must leave owner equal to A; the mutant, lacking the onlyOwner check, lets a non-owner overwrite owner, breaking this rule.

For any address actor, after ownership is transferred to actor and owned() is invoked by that actor, the stored owner must remain unchanged by owned() (owned() must not mutate ownership); the mutant overwrites owner inside owned(), and although here it only assigns msg.sender, the rule 'owned() does not change c.owner()' is the invariant the fuzzer-driven call checks.

For every possible caller, invoking owned() must either revert or leave ownership untouched: no input can make the owner getter return anything other than the value established by transferOwnership (initially address(0)); the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender inside owned(), so a call that reaches the body seizes/rewrites ownership, breaking the freeze rule for some caller.

For any caller, driving the contract through owned() must leave the ownership state readable via c.owner() exactly as last established by transferOwnership; owned() must be ownership-neutral, whereas the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender inside owned().

For any fuzzed actor, after ownership is transferred to that actor and they invoke owned(), the stored owner must remain exactly that transferred address and no non-owner caller may alter it; the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender inside owned(), so a call reaching the body rewrites ownership and breaks the freeze rule.

After the owner is explicitly transferred to any fuzzed actor, invoking owned() must be ownership-neutral: c.owner() remains exactly the address established by transferOwnership; the mutant overwrites owner inside owned(), so a call reaching the body rewrites ownership and breaks this invariant.
For any caller, calling owned() must revert unless the caller is the owner; the reference always reverts for non-owners, while the mutant lets any caller succeed.

property_summary: For any caller, calling owned() succeeds exactly when the caller is the current owner (c.owner()) and reverts otherwise; the mutant inverts the guard so the owner's call reverts.

For any caller authorised as owner and any newOwner, after transferOwnership(newOwner) the getter c.owner() must equal newOwner; the mutant never updates owner, so for some newOwner it still returns the old value.

For any caller who is the current owner, transferOwnership(newOwner) must always complete and leave owner() == newOwner for every newOwner, including address(0); the mutant reverts when newOwner == address(0), leaving owner unchanged.
